text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
NASA BORBA

- Serbian financial inspectorate blocks Nasa Borba publisher Fininvest's account. "Attempt to stop our newspaper is a threat to all independent media," says Nasa Borba director in a letter to Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.

- Senior Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) delegation on visit to Montenegro greeted with eggs and jeers. Protests in Podgorica against Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic and Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic.
- Milosevic violates the constitution or the law every day, says Serbian constitutional court judge Slobodan Vucetic.
- Several thousand workers of Zastava arms factory of Kragujevac protest outside city council, call on students and other workers to join them and march to Belgrade.
- Nominations for president of Serbia to be submitted by the end of August, for members of parliament by September 6.
- Opposition parties to decide on participation in republican elections on September 21 by mid August.
- Continuation of talks with the London Club of creditors could influence "recovery" of price of Yugoslavia's debt.
- Balkan power companies meet in Athens to discuss links with western European high-voltage networks.
- Sulejman Ugljanin's defence lawyers call for urgent intervention by the justice ministry against investigation of the leader of the Moslem National Council of Sandzak.
POLITIKA
- Serbian election commission adopts time schedule for election procedure in republican presidential and parliamentary elections set for September 21.

- SPS delegation said in talks with ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro it hoped the crisis in the Montenegrin leaderhsip would be overcome soon in keeping with the will of the DPS membership and the majority of the citizens of the republic.
- Sixth session of Yugoslav-Macedonian border commissions in Skopje on July 29-31.

- Weather permitting, wheat harvest will be complete within 3-4 days. Around 2.3 million tonnes of new wheat stockpiled in silos. Average yield per hectare 3.8 tonnes, says Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce official Milan Prostran.
BORBA
- Around 360 newly appointed judges and public prosecutors sworn in before Serbian parliament speaker Dragan Tomic.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT founds three charter companies, Air Yugoslavia, Air Pristina and Air Budva.
- Pristina district public prosecutor's office raises charges against 21 members of Albanian terrorist organisation "Liberation Army of Kosova"; 18 detained, three at large.

- Transformation of capital of public enterprises possible, but with founder retaining controlling package of shares, says Yugoslav railways assistant general manager for legal affairs Slavoljub Vuksanovic.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- After talks with SPS delegation, Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic said the two delegations reached a "high degree of consent on development of cooperation with the SPS."

- Zoran Lilic, SPS Vice President, said after talks with Bulatovic the goal of the visit to Podgorica was "to strengthen relations between the DPS and the SPS". Lilic said SPS will not abandon initiative to change the federal constitution.

- Several thousand rally in protests organised by the civic resistance movement of Montenegro "The Public against Fascism" against SPS visit to Podgorica. SPS delegation's cars showered with eggs and kicked in.

- "It is not only a question of what kind of Yugoslavia we want. It is important to ensure that Montenegro is an equal and dignified part of that Yugoslavia, that it can influence its economic and political profile," said Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.

- The Hague War Crimes Tribunal has expressed interest in the case of the deportation of 50 Moslem refugees from Montenegro to the Bosnian Serb republic in 1992 when present Yugoslav Defence Minister Pavle Bulatovic was the interior minister, said Montenegrin State Prosecutor Vladimir Susovic. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4305
